reference_title: Assuring Quality in Geotechnical Reporting Documents
chapter_title: Implementation of Quality Assurance for Geotechnical Reporting Documents

sections.title: QA Program Implementation, Checklists, and Documentation
sections.summary: QA program for GRDs uses checklists derived from or adapted from FHWA (2003) Checklists and Guidelines. Most DOTs have adapted these checklists or developed their own based on local practice. FHWA 2003 checklists cover 8 categories but are outdated for DB, GDRs, and newer technologies (micropiles, soil nailing, CFA piles). The General Information Form (GIF) in Appendix C serves as a cover sheet for any GRD QA review, identifying ACM, ADM, GRD type, reviewer, and project elements. Four QA process steps: (1) GRD preparation; (2) QC by GS; (3) QA review by GS; (4) project/program audit. Additional resources: GeoTechTools.org (SHRP2), FHWA GECs, FHWA website.
sections.body:
Owner agency QA programs: Based on interviews with DOTs, checklists are not consistently used, but where used, they are commonly derived from FHWA (2003) or developed from scratch. QA program requirements are essentially the same for all ACMs and ADMs, with few exceptions.

FHWA (2003) Checklists: Focus on site investigation, geotechnical features (embankments/cuts, landslides, retaining structures, structure foundations, ground improvement), and GRD development. Can be used directly or adapted. Limitations: do not cover DB ACM, GDRs, or newer technologies (micropiles, soil nailing, CFA piles). New checklists should be developed for these topics.

General Information Form (GIF, Appendix C, Exhibit C-7): Two-page cover for QA reviews. Documents: project title, contracting method (DBB/DB/CM/GC), QA reviewer and firm, GRD title, GRD type (GR/GDR/GBR/memo/email), GRD author and firm, author's client (owner/contractor/other), project components covered, design development stage (planning/preliminary/final), QA review level (discipline review vs. project audit). Review comments attached. Checklists attached.

Checklist content requirements: (1) documentation of assumptions — loads, load combinations for strength/service/extreme limit states, performance requirements; (2) documentation of calculations/analyses checked by GS of record (available upon request or included); (3) verification of exploration log procedures (owner standards, AASHTO, ASTM); (4) GRD limitation statement — allows GS to review plans and specs before construction.

Four QA process steps: (1) GRD preparation by project GS; (2) QC by GS of record or qualified representative; (3) QA review by independent GS; (4) project/program audit verifying QA reviews completed across all disciplines. Step 4 auditor need not be a GS.

State DOT examples: Florida DOT (FDOT) Soils and Foundation Handbook — detailed procedures for investigation, lab testing, classification, instrumentation, analysis, design, and GRD presentation. Utah DOT (UDOT) Manual of Instruction — defines GRD requirements; separate QC Checklists described as 'a tool to assist the project team' but 'cannot replace sound judgment.' North Carolina DOT (NCDOT) Guidelines & Procedures Manual — patterned after FHWA 2003 with DB updates; states 'the importance of preparing adequate geotechnical documents cannot be overstressed.' Additional resources: GeoTechTools.org (SHRP2, 50+ technologies with QC/QA procedures); FHWA GECs and other technical publications.
key_points: FHWA (2003) checklists widely used but need updating for DB, GDRs, micropiles, soil nailing, CFA piles
General Information Form (GIF) covers any GRD QA review — identifies ACM, ADM, reviewer, GRD type, design stage
Four QA steps: prepare → QC by GS → QA review → project audit (auditor need not be GS)
Checklists must document: assumptions, calculations (checked and available), exploration log procedures, GRD limitations
GS of record must review final PS&E to verify recommendations incorporated before acceptance by owner
GeoTechTools.org (SHRP2) provides QC/QA procedures for 50+ technologies
